cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Choose the Precedent
cards.instruction: Make someone choose which rule, custom, or prior decision will govern what happens now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. The handbook says lock the hall at six. Our festival permit says stay open till eight. Which governs tonight?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Keep the front open and lock the back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. So the permit governs public access, and the handbook governs everything else?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. Including the kitchen closing at six.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then are we canceling the seven-o'clock supper, or does the permit govern kitchens too?

mechanism: A controls the immediate action until B chooses which competing precedent will govern it, treating compromises as proposals for A conditional acceptance.
confusable: Ordinary indecision is confusable: A insists B select a governing rule, and tests whether the proposed rule actually resolves the next concrete consequence.
comparison: Hall opening tests a handbook/permit compromise against supper service; family seating tests elders/birthday traditions against a single pudding.
seedUse: Both full cards and all four canonical seeds read. Preserve actual competing rules and B practical compromises; let A permission over opening or serving make the rule choice consequential.
